title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 1st District
area: Eastern North Carolina, including Elizabeth City, Rocky Mount and Goldsboro.

context.text: North Carolina redrew its congressional district boundaries in October 2025, and District 1 is now rated R+5 on the Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index under the new lines. Incumbent Donald Davis (D) is seeking re-election against Laurie Buckhout (R) and Tom Bailey (L).

candidates.name: Donald Davis

summary.text: Don Davis is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, now redrawn to lean more Republican. He is an Air Force veteran, educator and former state senator serving his second term in Congress, where he is ranking member of the Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development.

background.text: Born and raised in Snow Hill, North Carolina; graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in 1994 and served eight years as an Air Force officer, including duties coordinating Air Force One and CODEL operations.

Taught national security affairs, military history and leadership as an assistant professor of Aerospace Studies at East Carolina University's Air Force ROTC detachment; was an educator for over 20 years.
Became the youngest mayor of Snow Hill at age 29, serving seven years, before being elected to the North Carolina State Senate in 2008, where he served 12 years.
Holds a bachelor's degree in social sciences from the U.S. Air Force Academy and a master's degree in administration from Central Michigan University.

record.text: Serves as ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, and as vice ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, also sitting on its Readiness and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.

candidates.name: Laurie Buckhout

summary.text: Laurie Buckhout is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Donald Davis in North Carolina's redrawn 1st Congressional District. She is a retired U.S. Army colonel and combat veteran who founded her own business after leaving the military.

background.text: Born in Virginia and lives in Edenton, North Carolina.

Earned a bachelor's degree from James Madison University, a master's of military arts and science in national military strategy, and a master's of science in information management from Webster University.
Served in the U.S. Army, reaching the rank of Colonel, including combat service; after leaving the military she founded her own business.

priorities.text: Lowering costs and cutting taxes for families in Eastern North Carolina.
Border security, including resourcing border patrol agents.
Cutting regulations affecting farmers and fishermen, and supporting the military and veterans.

positions.summary: Says she will stand strong against additional restrictions on law-abiding gun owners, citing her background as a combat veteran defending the right to keep and bear arms.
Says she will focus on ensuring border patrol agents have the resources they need to keep drugs out of the country.

candidates.researchNotes: Buckhout has not held elected office, so there is no voting or bill-sponsorship record; positions are drawn from her campaign website as summarized by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Tom Bailey
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Tom Bailey is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 1st Congressional District. He is a Vietnam veteran and longtime Libertarian Party activist focused on ballot access and election law.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 1968 to 1971; earned a high school diploma from South Bakersfield High School and graduated from the University of North Carolina, Wilmington in 1993.
Served on the Libertarian Party of North Carolina Executive Committee and as chairman of its Legal Action Committee, where he helped lead the federal ballot-access lawsuit McLoughlin v. Marsh.

priorities.text: Restoring voting rights of citizens to put control of government back in the hands of the people.
Major federal tax reform limiting the federal government to taxing only state governments.
Restoring the Bill of Rights with an emphasis on due process.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Bailey's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website was located.
